children: won dismissal of a lawsuit accusing the candy maker of misleading consumers by selling Reese’s Halloween-themed peanut butter pumpkins without the decorative facial carvings shown on the packaging.

U.S. District Judge Melissa Damian in Miami ruled that Florida residents Nathan Vidal and Eduardo Granados lacked legal standing to pursue claims that they had overpaid for the candy after discovering the pumpkins were faceless.

The plaintiffs said they bought the Reese’s products in part for the novelty of the “cool and beautiful carved-out designs” depicted on the packaging, including eyes and mouths. But Damian said their allegations amounted to subjective disappointment and did not establish that the pumpkins were defective, worthless, or had lost their economic value because they lacked the carvings.
The judge also rejected the plaintiffs’ attempt to show they paid as much as 25% too much by comparing Reese’s prices at Target
online stores. The plaintiffs had purchased their candy at Publix, the ruling said.

had argued that the packaging contained a disclaimer describing the carvings as a “decorating suggestion.” The company said a reasonable consumer would not interpret the images as a guarantee that the designs would appear on the candy itself.
The plaintiffs’ lawyer, James Kelly, said his clients remained disappointed and planned to appeal.
Damian had dismissed an earlier version of the lawsuit last September. Last month, Hershey
introduced more than 20 Halloween-themed products, including Reese’s pumpkins.

title: Hershey wins court fight over Reese’s Halloween pumpkin packaging
